paper_metadata.title: The microstructure and properties of Ti-Mo-Nb alloys for biomedical application

evidence.quote: A group of Ti–10Mo–nNb alloys (n = 3, 7, 10) were prepared using arc melting and graphite mould casting.
All the Ti–Mo–Nb alloys had much higher Vickers hardness values (394–441 HV) than that of c.p. Ti (160 HV).
The bending strength of Ti–10Mo–10Nb was higher than that of c.p.Ti (884 MPa) and lower than that of Ti–6Al–4V (1860 MPa)[10].

The ingots were remelted thrice prior to casting to improve chemical homogeneity.
The dimension of as-cast sample is Φ12 mm× 25 mm.
